study: Cavalluzzo et al. 2014 (TERC 'Using Data' math data-use PD)
eval_evidence: Evaluation conducted and authored by CNA Corporation (a third-party research firm) under IES Grant R305A100445; TERC developed the program, CNA evaluated it (title page; report no. CNA IRM-2013-U-006508).
developer_evidence: Two TERC facilitators delivered the professional development directly: 'Two TERC facilitators worked with the data teams'; 'facilitators from TERC used grade 4 data...'; facilitator logs each time a TERC facilitator conducted a PD/TA event.
cascade_evidence: TERC facilitators trained the school data teams (designated data coach + 4 grade 4/5 math teachers) directly, including the teachers themselves; the within-school 'data coach' is a team facilitation role, not an intermediary trainer who re-delivers the PD to the teachers.
counterfactual_evidence: Comparison = business-as-usual control schools (no Using Data PD); design/notes describe 30 control vs 30 treatment schools with no alternative data-use program.
coaching_evidence: Support was periodic TERC facilitator visits / school technical-assistance sessions (in-person plus phone/web), described as one to two hours at a school plus a few visits per year; data-team facilitation and resource suggestions, not recurring in-class instructional coaching cycles.
student_dose_evidence: Intervention is teacher-/data-team-facing PD on collaborative data use; only the teachers' regular math instruction is affected, no student-facing tutoring or extra dose.
maturity_evidence: Two-year rollout (SY 2011-12 and 2012-13); confirmatory student-achievement outcome measured at end of Year 2 (spring 2013), so teachers had a prior implementation year. (Year-1 student results reported only as exploratory.)
